what_happened: The job was meant to check the declared build-input sets (the athena-bin hashFiles globs in ci.yml and BUILD_PATHS) against the real compiled-in inputs. It was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier did not finish: it hit its 2400s deadline. All 5 acceptance criteria were reported unmet: the CHANGELOG root-cause entry, the new athena-core test deriving inputs from include_str!/include_bytes! targets, the negative fixture test, the workspace test/clippy/fmt criterion, and the no-replay-impact criterion. One check failed, `test`, with no output stored. A check is not a criterion. The event lists no blocker or major findings. So the stored fields do not show whether the work was wrong or the criteria were simply never judged. The failed `test` check also gives no baseline for whether the job caused it.
cause: The verifier runs under one fixed time limit. That limit must cover a full workspace test run plus judging each criterion. Nothing separates a timeout from a real failure, and nothing keeps partial verdicts, so the criteria it did judge are lost. The job's criteria are also heavy: they require the whole workspace test, clippy and fmt gate, a negative fixture test, and a read of ci.yml. Nothing sizes that verification against the deadline, and nothing reuses the check results that already ran. A failed `test` check with no baseline then blocks everything. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the verifier's progress.
prevention: Make verifier timeouts a distinct outcome from rejection. Record each criterion's verdict as soon as it is judged, and keep the partial results. On a deadline, hold the job for a resume. The resume should judge only the remaining criteria and reuse the check output already collected, and not rerun everything. Run the full gate once, before the verifier, and hand its output to the verifier as evidence. Also store the failing `test` check's output and compare it with a baseline from main, so the cause of the failure can be told apart from the job.
proposed_request: Make a verifier deadline a hold and not a rejection. (1) When the verifier reaches its time limit, record the job as held for verifier timeout, and not as rejected with every criterion unmet. (2) Write each criterion's verdict to the job record as soon as it is judged, so partial verdicts survive. (3) Add a resume path that judges only the unjudged criteria and reuses the already collected check output. (4) Store the output of any failed check, and compare it with a run of the same check on the base commit, so the final verdict states whether the job caused the failure. Acceptance: a test with a fake verifier that exceeds its deadline after judging 2 of 5 criteria shows a held job with those 2 verdicts kept. A resume run judges the other 3 only. A real failed check is still rejected, and the record includes its output and the baseline result.
